title: Red blood cell count

review.note: Drafted from the source below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

measures: A red blood cell (RBC) count measures the number of red blood cells in your blood. These cells carry oxygen from your lungs to every cell in your body.
context: This test is almost always part of a complete blood count and is used to help look at red blood cell disorders such as anemia. Pregnancy, living at a high altitude, and misuse of certain drugs for athletic performance can also change the count.
aboveRange: Can be associated with heart conditions, lung conditions, or scarring of the lungs often linked to cigarette smoking
Can be associated with polycythemia vera, kidney cancer, or sleep apnea
belowRange: Blood loss from injury or other causes
Can be associated with leukemia, multiple myeloma, or kidney failure
nextStep: Discuss this result with your doctor.
